\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{خطاب} (khiṭāb)}{خطاب (khiṭāb)}]{\ar{خطاب} (khiṭāb) — a speech, an address}

\label{lesson:AR-C357-khitab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a photographer, then the Arabic for to cover.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{خطاب}}
\textbf{\ar{خطاب}} — \emph{khiṭāb} — \textquotedblleft{}a speech, an address\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{خطاب} \ar{المدير} \ar{قصيرا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna khiṭāb al-mudīr qaṣīran.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The manager’s speech was short.
\end{quote}

In some countries \ar{خطاب} is also a letter.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{خطاب}} (\emph{khiṭāb}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-ṭ-b} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to address, to speak to\textquotedblright{}, the root of \emph{khaṭaba} and \emph{khuṭūba}. \emph{Khiṭāb} is the address itself.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khiṭāb}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khiṭāb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna khiṭāb al-mudīr qaṣīran.} — The manager’s speech was short.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a photographer, then the Arabic for to cover, then say \emph{khiṭāb} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{خطاب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A speech, an address\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ألقى} (alqā)}{ألقى (alqā)}]{\ar{ألقى} (alqā) — to deliver a speech; to throw}

\label{lesson:AR-C357-alqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to cover, then the Arabic for a speech.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ألقى}}
\textbf{\ar{ألقى}} — \emph{alqā} — \textquotedblleft{}to deliver a speech; to throw\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ألقت} \ar{الطالبة} \ar{كلمة} \ar{في} \ar{الحفل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{alqat aṭ-ṭāliba kalima fī al-ḥafl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The student gave a speech at the ceremony.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يلقي}, \emph{yulqī}.

\ar{ألقى} \ar{خطابا}, \ar{محاضرة}: to give a speech, a lecture. \ar{ألقى} \ar{القبض} \ar{على}: to arrest.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ألقى}} (\emph{alqā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{l-q-y} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to meet\textquotedblright{}, the root of \emph{liqāʾ}, a meeting, as in the taught \emph{ilā l-liqāʾ}. Form IV \emph{alqā} is \textquotedblleft{}to cast a thing so that it meets the ground\textquotedblright{}, and words cast to listeners.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{alqā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{alqā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{alqat aṭ-ṭāliba kalima fī al-ḥafl.} — The student gave a speech at the ceremony.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to cover, then the Arabic for a speech, then say \emph{alqā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ألقى} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To deliver a speech; to throw\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انعقد} (inʿaqada)}{انعقد (inʿaqada)}]{\ar{انعقد} (inʿaqada) — to convene, to be held}

\label{lesson:AR-C357-inaqada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a speech, then the Arabic for to deliver a speech.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انعقد}}
\textbf{\ar{انعقد}} — \emph{inʿaqada} — \textquotedblleft{}to convene, to be held\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انعقد} \ar{الاجتماع} \ar{في} \ar{الفندق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{inʿaqada al-ijtimāʿ fī al-funduq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The meeting was held at the hotel.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينعقد}, \emph{yanʿaqid}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انعقد}} (\emph{inʿaqada}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-q-d} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to tie a knot\textquotedblright{}, the root of the taught \emph{ʿaqd}, a contract. It is Form VII, \textquotedblleft{}to be tied\textquotedblright{}: a meeting is tied together.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inʿaqada}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inʿaqada}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inʿaqada al-ijtimāʿ fī al-funduq.} — The meeting was held at the hotel.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a speech, then the Arabic for to deliver a speech, then say \emph{inʿaqada} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{انعقد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To convene, to be held\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{افتتح} (iftataḥa)}{افتتح (iftataḥa)}]{\ar{افتتح} (iftataḥa) — to inaugurate, to open officially}

\label{lesson:AR-C357-iftataha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to deliver a speech, then the Arabic for to convene.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{افتتح}}
\textbf{\ar{افتتح}} — \emph{iftataḥa} — \textquotedblleft{}to inaugurate, to open officially\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{افتتح} \ar{الوزير} \ar{مستشفى} \ar{جديدا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iftataḥa al-wazīr mustashfā jadīdan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The minister opened a new hospital.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يفتتح}, \emph{yaftatiḥ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{افتتح}} (\emph{iftataḥa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-t-ḥ} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to open\textquotedblright{}, the root of the taught \emph{fataḥa}. It is Form VIII, \textquotedblleft{}to make a beginning\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iftataḥa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iftataḥa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iftataḥa al-wazīr mustashfā jadīdan.} — The minister opened a new hospital.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to deliver a speech, then the Arabic for to convene, then say \emph{iftataḥa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{افتتح} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To inaugurate, to open officially\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اختتم} (ikhtatama)}{اختتم (ikhtatama)}]{\ar{اختتم} (ikhtatama) — to conclude, to bring to a close}

\label{lesson:AR-C357-ikhtatama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to convene, then the Arabic for to inaugurate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اختتم}}
\textbf{\ar{اختتم}} — \emph{ikhtatama} — \textquotedblleft{}to conclude, to bring to a close\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اختتمت} \ar{المدرسة} \ar{السنة} \ar{بحفل} \ar{كبير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ikhtatamat al-madrasa as-sana bi-ḥafl kabīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The school ended the year with a big party.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يختتم}, \emph{yakhtatim}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اختتم}} (\emph{ikhtatama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-t-m} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to seal; to finish\textquotedblright{}, the root of the taught \emph{khātam}, a ring that seals. It is Form VIII, \textquotedblleft{}to bring to an end\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ikhtatama}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ikhtatama}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ikhtatamat al-madrasa as-sana bi-ḥafl kabīr.} — The school ended the year with a big party.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to convene, then the Arabic for to inaugurate, then say \emph{ikhtatama} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
